lld-approach.tldr:
• Clarify requirements, model entities, define relationships, choose patterns, code core-out, walk a scenario.
  • Graded on modelling, extensibility, correctness, concurrency and code quality.
  • Keep storage in-memory behind repository interfaces.
  • Working code at 60 minutes beats a perfect unfinished design.
lld-approach.body:
LLD rounds come in two shapes: a design discussion (45–60 min: classes, relationships, patterns, a few key methods) and machine coding (90–120 min: working, runnable code with a demo main). Both are graded on the same things.

What interviewers score

Criterion What good looks like
Requirement clarity you list features, ask about edge cases, and agree on scope before coding
Modelling entities map to the domain; responsibilities are clear (SRP)
Extensibility new vehicle type / payment mode / strategy added without editing existing classes (OCP)
Patterns used where they solve a real problem, not sprinkled for show
Correctness it runs, handles edge cases, validates input
Concurrency thread-safety where the domain demands it (seat booking, parking spots)
Code quality naming, small methods, enums over strings, immutability, custom exceptions

The 6-step routine

  1. Clarify requirements (5 min): write 5–7 functional bullets; mark what's out of scope.
  2. Identify entities — nouns in the requirements become classes; verbs become methods.
  3. Define relationships — is-a (inheritance/interfaces), has-a (composition), uses (dependency). Draw a quick class diagram.
  4. Pick patterns where variation exists: Strategy for interchangeable algorithms, State for lifecycle-driven behaviour, Factory for creation by type, Observer for notifications, Singleton for a single coordinator (sparingly).
  5. Code from the core outward: models and enums → services → a driver/demo. Keep storage in-memory behind repository interfaces.
  6. Walk through a scenario, then discuss extensions and concurrency.

SOLID in one LLD sentence each

Principle What it looks like in a machine-coding round
Single responsibility Ticket holds data; FeeCalculator computes the fee; ParkingService orchestrates
Open/closed a new PricingStrategy or vehicle type is a new class, not an edit to a switch
Liskov substitution every Spot subtype can be used wherever Spot is expected without surprises
Interface segregation Payable and Refundable instead of one fat PaymentProcessor
Dependency inversion services depend on SpotRepository / Clock / IntSupplier dice, injected through constructors

Layering that keeps code clean

Text
model/       Vehicle, Spot, Ticket ...        (data + invariants)
strategy/    SpotAllocationStrategy, PricingStrategy
repository/  in-memory maps behind interfaces
service/     ParkingService (orchestrates use cases)
exception/   SpotNotAvailableException ...
Main         demo scenario

Interview tip say "I'll keep storage in-memory behind a repository interface so it can be swapped for a database" — it signals separation of concerns without wasting time on persistence.

Pattern quick reference for LLD

Pattern Typical LLD use
Strategy pricing, spot allocation, split types, elevator scheduling, eviction policy
State vending machine, elevator, order/booking lifecycle
Factory create vehicles/spots/payment handlers by type
Observer notify display boards, subscribers, users
Singleton the system coordinator (prefer DI in real code)
Builder objects with many optional fields (bookings, requests)
Command undo/redo, queued elevator requests
Chain of responsibility ATM cash dispensing, request validation pipelines
Decorator add-ons to a base price (pizza toppings, insurance)

lld-parkinglot.tldr:
• Strategy for spot allocation and pricing; enums map vehicles to spot sizes.
  • Claim spots with an atomic CAS so concurrent gates never double-assign.
  • Track active tickets in a concurrent map; unpark once.
  • Extensions: EV spots, reservations, display boards via Observer.
lld-parkinglot.body:
Requirements: multiple floors; spot sizes (small, medium, large); vehicles (bike, car, truck) park in a fitting spot; issue a ticket on entry; compute fee on exit by duration and vehicle type; show free spots per floor; multiple entry/exit gates operating concurrently.

Patterns: Strategy (allocation: nearest-first, per-floor balancing; pricing: hourly, flat, weekend), Factory/enum mapping for vehicle → required spot size. Concurrency: two gates must not assign the same spot → atomic tryOccupy with CAS.

Java
enum SpotSize { SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE }

enum VehicleType {
    BIKE(SpotSize.SMALL), CAR(SpotSize.MEDIUM), TRUCK(SpotSize.LARGE);
    final SpotSize needs;
    VehicleType(SpotSize needs) { this.needs = needs; }
}

record Vehicle(String plate, VehicleType type) {}

final class Spot {
    final String id; final int floor; final SpotSize size;
    private final AtomicReference<Vehicle> occupant = new AtomicReference<>();
    Spot(String id, int floor, SpotSize size) { this.id = id; this.floor = floor; this.size = size; }

    boolean fits(Vehicle v) { return size.ordinal() >= v.type().needs.ordinal(); }  // larger spots can host smaller vehicles
    boolean isFree() { return occupant.get() == null; }
    boolean tryOccupy(Vehicle v) { return fits(v) && occupant.compareAndSet(null, v); } // atomic: no double booking
    void release() { occupant.set(null); }
}

record Ticket(String id, Vehicle vehicle, Spot spot, Instant entry) {}
record Receipt(Ticket ticket, Instant exit, long amountPaise) {}

interface SpotAllocationStrategy { Optional<Spot> allocate(List<Spot> spots, Vehicle v); }

/** Nearest floor first; prefers the smallest spot that fits so large spots stay available. */
class NearestSmallestFitStrategy implements SpotAllocationStrategy {
    public Optional<Spot> allocate(List<Spot> spots, Vehicle v) {
        return spots.stream()
            .filter(s -> s.isFree() && s.fits(v))
            .sorted(Comparator.comparingInt((Spot s) -> s.floor).thenComparing(s -> s.size))
            .filter(s -> s.tryOccupy(v))          // first one we win the CAS on
            .findFirst();
    }
}

interface PricingStrategy { long price(Ticket t, Instant exit); }

class HourlyPricing implements PricingStrategy {
    private final Map<VehicleType, Long> perHourPaise = Map.of(
        VehicleType.BIKE, 2_000L, VehicleType.CAR, 5_000L, VehicleType.TRUCK, 10_000L);
    public long price(Ticket t, Instant exit) {
        long minutes = Math.max(1, Duration.between(t.entry(), exit).toMinutes());
        long hours = (minutes + 59) / 60;                        // round up partial hours
        return hours * perHourPaise.get(t.vehicle().type());
    }
}

class ParkingFullException extends RuntimeException {
    ParkingFullException(VehicleType t) { super("No spot available for " + t); }
}

public class ParkingLot {
    private final List<Spot> spots;
    private final SpotAllocationStrategy allocation;
    private final PricingStrategy pricing;
    private final Map<String, Ticket> active = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Clock clock;

    public ParkingLot(List<Spot> spots, SpotAllocationStrategy a, PricingStrategy p, Clock clock) {
        this.spots = List.copyOf(spots); this.allocation = a; this.pricing = p; this.clock = clock;
    }

    public Ticket park(Vehicle v) {
        Spot spot = allocation.allocate(spots, v).orElseThrow(() -> new ParkingFullException(v.type()));
        Ticket t = new Ticket(UUID.randomUUID().toString(), v, spot, clock.instant());
        active.put(t.id(), t);
        return t;
    }

    public Receipt unpark(String ticketId) {
        Ticket t = active.remove(ticketId);                     // atomic: a ticket can be closed once
        if (t == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown or already closed ticket " + ticketId);
        Instant exit = clock.instant();
        t.spot().release();
        return new Receipt(t, exit, pricing.price(t, exit));
    }

    public Map<Integer, Long> freeSpotsByFloor() {
        return spots.stream().filter(Spot::isFree)
            .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(s -> s.floor, TreeMap::new, Collectors.counting()));
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Spot> spots = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int f = 0; f < 2; f++) {
            for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) spots.add(new Spot("F" + f + "-S" + i, f, SpotSize.SMALL));
            for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) spots.add(new Spot("F" + f + "-M" + i, f, SpotSize.MEDIUM));
            spots.add(new Spot("F" + f + "-L0", f, SpotSize.LARGE));
        }
        ParkingLot lot = new ParkingLot(spots, new NearestSmallestFitStrategy(), new HourlyPricing(), Clock.systemUTC());
        Ticket t = lot.park(new Vehicle("MH04AB1234", VehicleType.CAR));
        System.out.println("Parked at " + t.spot().id + " | free: " + lot.freeSpotsByFloor());
        System.out.println("Paid " + lot.unpark(t.id()).amountPaise() / 100.0 + " INR");
    }
}

Extensions to discuss: EV spots with chargers (new spot type + filter), reservations, display boards updated via Observer, multiple pricing rules (weekend/peak as Decorators over a base strategy), lost ticket flow, persistence behind repositories, gates as separate threads hammering park (the CAS keeps it safe).

lld-lru.tldr:
• LRU = HashMap + doubly linked list with sentinels: O(1) get and put.
  • Move to front on access; evict the tail when full.
  • LFU tracks frequency buckets and a running minimum frequency.
  • Production code uses Caffeine (W-TinyLFU).
lld-lru.body:
Requirements: get(key) and put(key, value) in O(1); capacity N; when full, evict the least recently used entry. Interviewers usually forbid LinkedHashMap.

Design: a HashMap<K, Node> for O(1) lookup + a doubly linked list ordered by recency (head = most recent, tail = least recent). Sentinel head/tail nodes remove null checks.

What happens on get(k2) and on put(k5) when full

Java
public class LruCache<K, V> {
    private final class Node {
        K key; V value; Node prev, next;
        Node(K k, V v) { key = k; value = v; }
    }

    private final int capacity;
    private final Map<K, Node> map;
    private final Node head = new Node(null, null), tail = new Node(null, null);

    public LruCache(int capacity) {
        if (capacity <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("capacity must be > 0");
        this.capacity = capacity;
        this.map = new HashMap<>(capacity * 2);
        head.next = tail; tail.prev = head;
    }

    public synchronized V get(K key) {
        Node n = map.get(key);
        if (n == null) return null;
        moveToFront(n);
        return n.value;
    }

    public synchronized void put(K key, V value) {
        Node n = map.get(key);
        if (n != null) { n.value = value; moveToFront(n); return; }
        if (map.size() == capacity) {
            Node lru = tail.prev;                 // evict least recently used
            unlink(lru);
            map.remove(lru.key);
        }
        n = new Node(key, value);
        map.put(key, n);
        addFirst(n);
    }

    private void moveToFront(Node n) { unlink(n); addFirst(n); }
    private void unlink(Node n) { n.prev.next = n.next; n.next.prev = n.prev; }
    private void addFirst(Node n) { n.next = head.next; n.prev = head; head.next.prev = n; head.next = n; }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        LruCache<Integer, String> c = new LruCache<>(2);
        c.put(1, "a"); c.put(2, "b");
        c.get(1);                   // 1 is now most recent
        c.put(3, "c");              // evicts 2
        System.out.println(c.get(2) + " " + c.get(1) + " " + c.get(3));   // null a c
    }
}

LFU in O(1): evict the least frequently used; ties broken by least recent. Keep key → node, freq → doubly linked list of nodes, and minFreq.

Java
public class LfuCache<K, V> {
    private record Entry<V>(V value, int freq) {}
    private final int capacity;
    private final Map<K, Entry<V>> entries = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<Integer, LinkedHashSet<K>> buckets = new HashMap<>();  // freq -> keys in LRU order
    private int minFreq;

    public LfuCache(int capacity) { this.capacity = capacity; }

    public synchronized V get(K key) {
        Entry<V> e = entries.get(key);
        if (e == null) return null;
        touch(key, e);
        return e.value();
    }

    public synchronized void put(K key, V value) {
        if (capacity == 0) return;
        Entry<V> e = entries.get(key);
        if (e != null) { entries.put(key, new Entry<>(value, e.freq())); touch(key, entries.get(key)); return; }
        if (entries.size() == capacity) {
            K evict = buckets.get(minFreq).iterator().next();     // oldest key with the lowest frequency
            buckets.get(minFreq).remove(evict);
            entries.remove(evict);
        }
        entries.put(key, new Entry<>(value, 1));
        buckets.computeIfAbsent(1, f -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).add(key);
        minFreq = 1;
    }

    private void touch(K key, Entry<V> e) {
        int f = e.freq();
        LinkedHashSet<K> b = buckets.get(f);
        b.remove(key);
        if (f == minFreq && b.isEmpty()) minFreq++;
        entries.put(key, new Entry<>(e.value(), f + 1));
        buckets.computeIfAbsent(f + 1, x -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).add(key);
    }
}

Discussion points: thread safety (one lock is simplest; segment the cache by key hash for throughput; Caffeine uses lock-free buffers and W-TinyLFU), TTL per entry, eviction policy as a Strategy, and metrics (hit ratio).

lld-splitwise.tldr:
• Split types (equal, exact, percent) are Strategies that validate their own input.
  • Store money as paise and assign rounding leftovers deterministically.
  • Keep net balances per user; simplify with a greedy creditor–debtor match (≤ n−1 transfers).
  • Optimal debt minimization is NP-hard.
lld-splitwise.body:
Requirements: users and groups; add an expense paid by one user and split among participants equally, by exact amounts, or by percentage; show balances (who owes whom); settle up; simplify debts to minimize the number of transactions.

Key modelling decisions: money as long paise (never double); each split type is a Strategy that validates its own input; the balance sheet keeps net balance per user (positive = is owed, negative = owes); rounding leftovers go to the first participant so totals always match.

Debt simplification — before and after

Compute each person's net balance, then repeatedly match the largest debtor with the largest creditor (two heaps). Each step settles at least one person, so there are at most n − 1 transfers.

Java
enum SplitType { EQUAL, EXACT, PERCENT }

interface SplitStrategy {
    /** @return paise owed by each participant; must sum to total. */
    Map<String, Long> split(long total, List<String> participants, List<Double> values);
}

class EqualSplit implements SplitStrategy {
    public Map<String, Long> split(long total, List<String> users, List<Double> ignored) {
        long share = total / users.size(), remainder = total % users.size();
        Map<String, Long> out = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < users.size(); i++) out.put(users.get(i), share + (i < remainder ? 1 : 0));
        return out;
    }
}

class ExactSplit implements SplitStrategy {
    public Map<String, Long> split(long total, List<String> users, List<Double> amounts) {
        long sum = 0; Map<String, Long> out = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < users.size(); i++) {
            long paise = Math.round(amounts.get(i) * 100);
            out.put(users.get(i), paise); sum += paise;
        }
        if (sum != total) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Exact amounts must add up to the total");
        return out;
    }
}

class PercentSplit implements SplitStrategy {
    public Map<String, Long> split(long total, List<String> users, List<Double> pcts) {
        double pctSum = pcts.stream().mapToDouble(Double::doubleValue).sum();
        if (Math.abs(pctSum - 100.0) > 1e-6) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Percentages must add up to 100");
        Map<String, Long> out = new LinkedHashMap<>(); long assigned = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < users.size(); i++) {
            long part = (long) Math.floor(total * pcts.get(i) / 100.0);
            out.put(users.get(i), part); assigned += part;
        }
        out.merge(users.get(0), total - assigned, Long::sum);   // rounding leftover
        return out;
    }
}

record Transfer(String from, String to, long paise) {}

public class ExpenseService {
    private final Map<SplitType, SplitStrategy> strategies = Map.of(
        SplitType.EQUAL, new EqualSplit(), SplitType.EXACT, new ExactSplit(), SplitType.PERCENT, new PercentSplit());
    private final Map<String, Long> net = new HashMap<>();        // + is owed, - owes

    public synchronized void addExpense(String paidBy, long totalPaise, SplitType type,
                                        List<String> participants, List<Double> values) {
        Map<String, Long> owed = strategies.get(type).split(totalPaise, participants, values);
        net.merge(paidBy, totalPaise, Long::sum);                       // payer fronted the money
        owed.forEach((user, amt) -> net.merge(user, -amt, Long::sum));  // each participant owes their share
    }

    /** Greedy: repeatedly match the biggest creditor with the biggest debtor. At most n-1 transfers. */
    public synchronized List<Transfer> simplify() {
        PriorityQueue<Map.Entry<String, Long>> creditors = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Long.compare(b.getValue(), a.getValue()));
        PriorityQueue<Map.Entry<String, Long>> debtors   = new PriorityQueue<>(Comparator.comparingLong((Map.Entry<String, Long> e) -> e.getValue()));
        net.forEach((u, v) -> {
            if (v > 0) creditors.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(u, v));
            else if (v < 0) debtors.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(u, v));
        });
        List<Transfer> result = new ArrayList<>();
        while (!creditors.isEmpty() && !debtors.isEmpty()) {
            var c = creditors.poll(); var d = debtors.poll();
            long amt = Math.min(c.getValue(), -d.getValue());
            result.add(new Transfer(d.getKey(), c.getKey(), amt));
            if (c.getValue() - amt > 0) creditors.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(c.getKey(), c.getValue() - amt));
            if (d.getValue() + amt < 0) debtors.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(d.getKey(), d.getValue() + amt));
        }
        return result;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        ExpenseService s = new ExpenseService();
        s.addExpense("nk", 120_000, SplitType.EQUAL, List.of("nk", "asha", "ravi"), List.of());   // 1200 dinner
        s.addExpense("asha", 60_000, SplitType.PERCENT, List.of("nk", "asha", "ravi"), List.of(50.0, 25.0, 25.0));
        s.simplify().forEach(t -> System.out.printf("%s pays %s %.2f%n", t.from(), t.to(), t.paise() / 100.0));
    }
}

Extensions: per-group balances (Map<groupId, Map<user, net>>), expense history and edit/delete (store expenses as events and recompute), currencies, notifications (Observer), and the note that optimal debt minimization is NP-hard — greedy gives at most n−1 transfers, which is what Splitwise-style apps use.

lld-elevator.tldr:
• Strategy for dispatch; elevators serve stops with the LOOK sweep.
  • Model direction and state explicitly; tick-driven simulation keeps it testable.
  • Prefer elevators already moving toward the call in the same direction.
  • Extensions: capacity, emergency modes, zoning.
lld-elevator.body:
Requirements: N elevators, M floors; hall calls (up/down buttons on a floor) and car calls (floor buttons inside); dispatch the best elevator; each elevator serves requests efficiently (SCAN/LOOK: keep going in one direction while there are requests ahead); door and movement states; extensible scheduling.

Patterns: Strategy for dispatch (nearest car, zoning, least busy); State for elevator states (IDLE, MOVING_UP, MOVING_DOWN, DOORS_OPEN); the simulation is driven by a step() tick so it's deterministic and testable.

LOOK scheduling — keep moving in the current direction while there are stops ahead, then reverse:

Java
enum Direction { UP, DOWN, IDLE }

record HallCall(int floor, Direction direction) {}

class Elevator {
    final int id;
    private int floor = 0;
    private Direction direction = Direction.IDLE;
    private final TreeSet<Integer> upStops = new TreeSet<>();
    private final TreeSet<Integer> downStops = new TreeSet<>();

    Elevator(int id) { this.id = id; }
    int floor() { return floor; }
    Direction direction() { return direction; }
    int pendingStops() { return upStops.size() + downStops.size(); }

    synchronized void addStop(int target) {
        if (target > floor) upStops.add(target);
        else if (target < floor) downStops.add(target);
        if (direction == Direction.IDLE && target != floor) direction = target > floor ? Direction.UP : Direction.DOWN;
    }

    /** One tick: move a floor, open doors when reaching a stop, LOOK algorithm for direction changes. */
    synchronized void step() {
        switch (direction) {
            case UP -> {
                floor++;
                if (upStops.remove(floor)) System.out.println("Elevator " + id + " stops at " + floor);
                if (upStops.isEmpty()) direction = downStops.isEmpty() ? Direction.IDLE : Direction.DOWN;
            }
            case DOWN -> {
                floor--;
                if (downStops.remove(floor)) System.out.println("Elevator " + id + " stops at " + floor);
                if (downStops.isEmpty()) direction = upStops.isEmpty() ? Direction.IDLE : Direction.UP;
            }
            case IDLE -> { }
        }
    }
}

interface DispatchStrategy { Elevator choose(List<Elevator> elevators, HallCall call); }

/** Prefer an elevator already moving toward the call in the same direction, else the nearest idle, else least busy. */
class NearestCarStrategy implements DispatchStrategy {
    public Elevator choose(List<Elevator> elevators, HallCall c) {
        return elevators.stream().min(Comparator.comparingInt(e -> cost(e, c))).orElseThrow();
    }
    private int cost(Elevator e, HallCall c) {
        int distance = Math.abs(e.floor() - c.floor());
        boolean onTheWay = (e.direction() == Direction.UP && c.direction() == Direction.UP && e.floor() <= c.floor())
                        || (e.direction() == Direction.DOWN && c.direction() == Direction.DOWN && e.floor() >= c.floor());
        if (e.direction() == Direction.IDLE) return distance;
        if (onTheWay) return distance;
        return distance + 2 * e.pendingStops() + 10;          // must finish current sweep first
    }
}

public class ElevatorController {
    private final List<Elevator> elevators = new ArrayList<>();
    private final DispatchStrategy strategy;

    public ElevatorController(int count, DispatchStrategy strategy) {
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) elevators.add(new Elevator(i));
        this.strategy = strategy;
    }
    public void hallCall(int floor, Direction dir) {
        Elevator e = strategy.choose(elevators, new HallCall(floor, dir));
        System.out.println("Hall call " + floor + " " + dir + " -> elevator " + e.id);
        e.addStop(floor);
    }
    public void carCall(int elevatorId, int floor) { elevators.get(elevatorId).addStop(floor); }
    public void step() { elevators.forEach(Elevator::step); }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        ElevatorController c = new ElevatorController(2, new NearestCarStrategy());
        c.hallCall(5, Direction.DOWN);
        c.hallCall(2, Direction.UP);
        for (int t = 0; t < 8; t++) c.step();
        c.carCall(1, 9);
        for (int t = 0; t < 8; t++) c.step();
    }
}

Extensions: capacity/weight limits, emergency stop and fire mode (State), express elevators/zoning (strategy), requests queued as Commands, a dedicated scheduler thread instead of manual step(), and fairness (max wait time).

lld-bookmyshow.tldr:
• Seat holds must be atomic and all-or-nothing.
  • Lock seats in a consistent order to avoid deadlocks; holds expire.
  • Confirm only if the hold is still valid; otherwise refund.
  • Distributed version: Redis SET NX EX holds plus a conditional SQL update.
lld-bookmyshow.body:
Requirements: browse cities → cinemas → shows; view the seat map; select seats and hold them for ~10 minutes while paying; confirm on payment or release on timeout/failure; no double booking under concurrent requests; pricing by seat category.

The core problem — concurrency on seats. Options:

Seat lifecycle

Approach How When
Pessimistic DB lock SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the seat rows inside a transaction single DB, moderate traffic
Optimistic lock version column; UPDATE ... WHERE status='AVAILABLE' AND version=? low contention
Conditional update UPDATE show_seats SET status='HELD' WHERE id IN (...) AND status='AVAILABLE'; check affected rows = requested simple and effective
Redis lock / SETNX per seat with TTL hold = key with 10-min TTL very high traffic, then persist on confirm

In-memory machine-coding version: lock the seats in a consistent order (sorted by id) so two users selecting overlapping seats can't deadlock, and make the hold all-or-nothing.

Java
enum SeatStatus { AVAILABLE, HELD, BOOKED }
enum BookingStatus { PENDING, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED }

final class ShowSeat {
    final String id; final long pricePaise;
    final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
    SeatStatus status = SeatStatus.AVAILABLE;
    String heldBy; Instant holdExpiry;
    ShowSeat(String id, long pricePaise) { this.id = id; this.pricePaise = pricePaise; }

    boolean isAvailable(Instant now) {
        return status == SeatStatus.AVAILABLE
            || (status == SeatStatus.HELD && holdExpiry.isBefore(now));   // expired holds count as free
    }
}

final class Booking {
    final String id = UUID.randomUUID().toString();
    final String userId; final String showId; final List<ShowSeat> seats; final long amountPaise;
    volatile BookingStatus status = BookingStatus.PENDING;
    Booking(String userId, String showId, List<ShowSeat> seats) {
        this.userId = userId; this.showId = showId; this.seats = seats;
        this.amountPaise = seats.stream().mapToLong(s -> s.pricePaise).sum();
    }
}

class SeatUnavailableException extends RuntimeException {
    SeatUnavailableException(String seat) { super("Seat " + seat + " is not available"); }
}

public class BookingService {
    private static final Duration HOLD = Duration.ofMinutes(10);
    private final Map<String, Map<String, ShowSeat>> seatsByShow = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Booking> bookings = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Clock clock;

    public BookingService(Clock clock) { this.clock = clock; }

    public void addShow(String showId, Map<String, Long> seatPrices) {
        Map<String, ShowSeat> m = new HashMap<>();
        seatPrices.forEach((id, price) -> m.put(id, new ShowSeat(id, price)));
        seatsByShow.put(showId, Map.copyOf(m));
    }

    public Booking hold(String showId, List<String> seatIds, String userId) {
        Map<String, ShowSeat> showSeats = seatsByShow.get(showId);
        List<ShowSeat> seats = seatIds.stream().sorted()                 // consistent lock order: no deadlocks
            .map(id -> Optional.ofNullable(showSeats.get(id)).orElseThrow(() -> new SeatUnavailableException(id)))
            .toList();
        seats.forEach(s -> s.lock.lock());
        try {
            Instant now = clock.instant();
            for (ShowSeat s : seats) if (!s.isAvailable(now)) throw new SeatUnavailableException(s.id); // all-or-nothing
            Booking b = new Booking(userId, showId, seats);
            for (ShowSeat s : seats) { s.status = SeatStatus.HELD; s.heldBy = b.id; s.holdExpiry = now.plus(HOLD); }
            bookings.put(b.id, b);
            return b;
        } finally {
            seats.forEach(s -> s.lock.unlock());
        }
    }

    public void confirm(String bookingId, String paymentRef) {
        Booking b = bookings.get(bookingId);
        lockAll(b);
        try {
            Instant now = clock.instant();
            for (ShowSeat s : b.seats)
                if (!bookingId.equals(s.heldBy) || s.holdExpiry.isBefore(now)) {
                    b.status = BookingStatus.EXPIRED;                    // trigger a refund for paymentRef
                    throw new IllegalStateException("Hold expired for booking " + bookingId);
                }
            b.seats.forEach(s -> s.status = SeatStatus.BOOKED);
            b.status = BookingStatus.CONFIRMED;
        } finally { unlockAll(b); }
    }

    public void release(String bookingId) {
        Booking b = bookings.get(bookingId);
        lockAll(b);
        try {
            for (ShowSeat s : b.seats)
                if (bookingId.equals(s.heldBy) && s.status == SeatStatus.HELD) { s.status = SeatStatus.AVAILABLE; s.heldBy = null; }
            b.status = BookingStatus.CANCELLED;
        } finally { unlockAll(b); }
    }

    private void lockAll(Booking b) { b.seats.stream().sorted(Comparator.comparing(s -> s.id)).forEach(s -> s.lock.lock()); }
    private void unlockAll(Booking b) { b.seats.forEach(s -> s.lock.unlock()); }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        BookingService svc = new BookingService(Clock.systemUTC());
        svc.addShow("show-1", Map.of("A1", 25_000L, "A2", 25_000L, "A3", 25_000L));
        ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2);
        Callable<String> u1 = () -> svc.hold("show-1", List.of("A1", "A2"), "nk").id;
        Callable<String> u2 = () -> svc.hold("show-1", List.of("A2", "A3"), "asha").id;
        for (Future<String> f : pool.invokeAll(List.of(u1, u2))) {
            try { System.out.println("held " + f.get()); }
            catch (ExecutionException e) { System.out.println("rejected: " + e.getCause().getMessage()); }
        }
        pool.shutdown();
    }
}

Extensions: expiry sweeper (scheduled task releasing expired holds, or lazy expiry as above), payment integration with idempotency, seat categories and dynamic pricing (Strategy), coupons (Decorator over price), waitlists, and the distributed version: Redis SET seat:{show}:{seat} bookingId NX EX 600 for holds and a conditional SQL update on confirm.

lld-vendingmachine.tldr:
• The State pattern: each state owns its legal actions and transitions.
  • Adding a state means a new class, not editing every switch.
  • Greedy change-making works for canonical coin systems.
  • Handle refunds when change can't be made.
lld-vendingmachine.body:
Requirements: select a product, insert coins/notes, dispense the product and change, cancel and refund, handle out-of-stock and insufficient funds. The machine's behaviour depends on what state it's in — the textbook State pattern.

Java
enum Coin { ONE(1), TWO(2), FIVE(5), TEN(10), TWENTY(20), FIFTY(50), HUNDRED(100);
    final int value; Coin(int v) { value = v; } }

record Product(String code, String name, int price) {}

interface State {
    default void select(VendingMachine m, String code) { throw new IllegalStateException("Cannot select now"); }
    default void insert(VendingMachine m, Coin c)      { throw new IllegalStateException("Select a product first"); }
    default void cancel(VendingMachine m)              { }
}

class IdleState implements State {
    public void select(VendingMachine m, String code) {
        if (m.stockOf(code) == 0) throw new IllegalStateException(code + " is out of stock");
        m.selected = m.product(code);
        m.setState(new HasSelectionState());
    }
}

class HasSelectionState implements State {
    public void insert(VendingMachine m, Coin c) {
        m.balance += c.value;
        if (m.balance >= m.selected.price()) m.dispense();
        else m.setState(new HasMoneyState());
    }
    public void cancel(VendingMachine m) { m.reset(); }
}

class HasMoneyState extends HasSelectionState {
    @Override public void cancel(VendingMachine m) {
        System.out.println("Refunding " + m.balance);
        m.reset();
    }
}

public class VendingMachine {
    private final Map<String, Product> products = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Integer> stock = new HashMap<>();
    private State state = new IdleState();
    Product selected;
    int balance;

    public void load(Product p, int qty) { products.put(p.code(), p); stock.merge(p.code(), qty, Integer::sum); }
    Product product(String code) { return Optional.ofNullable(products.get(code)).orElseThrow(); }
    int stockOf(String code) { return stock.getOrDefault(code, 0); }
    void setState(State s) { state = s; }

    public synchronized void select(String code) { state.select(this, code); }
    public synchronized void insert(Coin c)      { state.insert(this, c); }
    public synchronized void cancel()            { state.cancel(this); }

    void dispense() {
        stock.merge(selected.code(), -1, Integer::sum);
        int change = balance - selected.price();
        System.out.println("Dispensed " + selected.name() + (change > 0 ? ", change " + change + " = " + makeChange(change) : ""));
        reset();
    }
    void reset() { selected = null; balance = 0; state = new IdleState(); }

    /** Greedy change works for canonical coin systems like INR. */
    static List<Coin> makeChange(int amount) {
        List<Coin> out = new ArrayList<>();
        Coin[] coins = Coin.values();
        for (int i = coins.length - 1; i >= 0 && amount > 0; i--)
            while (amount >= coins[i].value) { out.add(coins[i]); amount -= coins[i].value; }
        return out;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        VendingMachine vm = new VendingMachine();
        vm.load(new Product("A1", "Coke", 40), 5);
        vm.select("A1"); vm.insert(Coin.TWENTY); vm.insert(Coin.FIFTY);   // Dispensed Coke, change 30
    }
}

Why State beats a switch: each state owns its legal transitions; adding a MaintenanceState means a new class, not edits to every switch. Extensions: finite coin inventory (change may be impossible → refund), card/UPI payment (Strategy), admin refill mode, and a real change-making DP for non-canonical coin sets.

lld-tictactoe.tldr:
• Row, column and diagonal counters give O(1) win detection.
  • Model turns with a queue of players.
  • Inject randomness (dice) for deterministic tests.
  • Snakes and ladders fit one jump map.
lld-tictactoe.body:
Game problems test clean modelling: board, players, turns, win detection, and extensibility (N×N board, more players, bots).

The counter trick on a 3×3 board — X adds +1, O adds −1:

Text
 X | X | X        rows  = [+3, -1,  0]   <- row 0 reached +3 = N  →  X wins
---+---+---       cols  = [ 1,  0,  1]
   | O |          diag  =  0 (X at 0,0 +1, O at 1,1 −1)
---+---+---       anti  =  0 (X at 0,2 +1, O at 1,1 −1)
   |   | O

Tic-Tac-Toe with O(1) win detection: instead of scanning the board after every move, keep counters per row, column and both diagonals. Player X adds +1, O adds −1; a counter reaching ±N means a win.

Java
enum Symbol { X, O }

record Player(String name, Symbol symbol) {}

public class TicTacToe {
    private final int n;
    private final Symbol[][] board;
    private final int[] rows, cols;
    private int diag, antiDiag, moves;
    private final Deque<Player> turns = new ArrayDeque<>();

    public TicTacToe(int n, Player p1, Player p2) {
        this.n = n; board = new Symbol[n][n]; rows = new int[n]; cols = new int[n];
        turns.add(p1); turns.add(p2);
    }

    /** @return the winner, or null if the game continues. Throws on illegal moves. */
    public Player move(int r, int c) {
        if (r < 0 || c < 0 || r >= n || c >= n || board[r][c] != null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid move");
        Player p = turns.poll();
        board[r][c] = p.symbol();
        int delta = p.symbol() == Symbol.X ? 1 : -1;
        rows[r] += delta; cols[c] += delta;
        if (r == c) diag += delta;
        if (r + c == n - 1) antiDiag += delta;
        moves++;
        turns.add(p);
        if (Math.abs(rows[r]) == n || Math.abs(cols[c]) == n || Math.abs(diag) == n || Math.abs(antiDiag) == n) return p;
        if (moves == n * n) System.out.println("Draw");
        return null;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        TicTacToe g = new TicTacToe(3, new Player("nk", Symbol.X), new Player("asha", Symbol.O));
        int[][] script = {{0,0},{1,1},{0,1},{2,2},{0,2}};
        for (int[] m : script) {
            Player w = g.move(m[0], m[1]);
            if (w != null) { System.out.println(w.name() + " wins"); break; }
        }
    }
}

Snake & Ladder in brief

Java
public class SnakeAndLadder {
    private final Map<Integer, Integer> jumps;          // snakes (head -> tail) and ladders (bottom -> top) in one map
    private final Map<String, Integer> positions = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    private final Deque<String> turns = new ArrayDeque<>();
    private final IntSupplier dice;                      // injectable for deterministic tests

    public SnakeAndLadder(Map<Integer, Integer> jumps, List<String> players, IntSupplier dice) {
        this.jumps = Map.copyOf(jumps); this.dice = dice;
        players.forEach(p -> { positions.put(p, 0); turns.add(p); });
    }

    public Optional<String> playTurn() {
        String p = turns.poll();
        int roll = dice.getAsInt(), next = positions.get(p) + roll;
        if (next <= 100) positions.put(p, jumps.getOrDefault(next, next));   // overshooting 100 = stay
        turns.add(p);
        return positions.get(p) == 100 ? Optional.of(p) : Optional.empty();
    }
}
// new SnakeAndLadder(Map.of(17, 7, 54, 34, 4, 14, 9, 31), List.of("nk", "asha"),
//                    () -> ThreadLocalRandom.current().nextInt(1, 7));

Design talking points: inject randomness (IntSupplier) for testability; validate the board (no cycles, no jump at 100); extend with multiple dice or "roll a 6 to start" as rule Strategies; players as an interface so a BotPlayer can plug in.

lld-kvstore.tldr:
• ConcurrentHashMap for data; DelayQueue for active expiry; check on read for lazy expiry.
  • Remove only if the expired entry is still the current one.
  • Extensions: LRU size limits, persistence, transactions, sharding.
  • Mirror Redis's expiry design.
lld-kvstore.body:
Requirements: put(key, value, ttl), get, delete; keys expire after their TTL; thread-safe; expired keys cleaned up without scanning the whole map on every call; optional: size limit with eviction and simple transactions.

Design: a ConcurrentHashMap for data + a DelayQueue (or a priority queue by expiry) drained by a background thread for active expiry, and a check on read for lazy expiry (like Redis).

Why the reaper compares expiresAt before removing — the overwrite race:

Java
public class TtlStore<K, V> implements AutoCloseable {
    private record Entry<V>(V value, long expiresAtNanos) {
        boolean expired(long now) { return expiresAtNanos > 0 && now >= expiresAtNanos; }
    }
    private record Expiry<K>(K key, long atNanos) implements Delayed {
        public long getDelay(TimeUnit unit) { return unit.convert(atNanos - System.nanoTime(), TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS); }
        public int compareTo(Delayed o) { return Long.compare(atNanos, ((Expiry<?>) o).atNanos); }
    }

    private final ConcurrentHashMap<K, Entry<V>> data = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final DelayQueue<Expiry<K>> expiries = new DelayQueue<>();
    private final Thread reaper;

    public TtlStore() {
        reaper = Thread.ofPlatform().daemon().name("ttl-reaper").start(() -> {
            try {
                while (!Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()) {
                    Expiry<K> e = expiries.take();                       // blocks until the earliest expiry is due
                    // remove only if this entry is still the one that expired (it may have been overwritten)
                    data.computeIfPresent(e.key(), (k, v) -> v.expiresAtNanos() == e.atNanos() ? null : v);
                }
            } catch (InterruptedException ignored) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); }
        });
    }

    public void put(K key, V value, Duration ttl) {
        long at = ttl == null ? 0 : System.nanoTime() + ttl.toNanos();
        data.put(key, new Entry<>(value, at));
        if (at > 0) expiries.add(new Expiry<>(key, at));
    }

    public Optional<V> get(K key) {
        Entry<V> e = data.get(key);
        if (e == null) return Optional.empty();
        if (e.expired(System.nanoTime())) {                              // lazy expiry
            data.remove(key, e);
            return Optional.empty();
        }
        return Optional.of(e.value());
    }

    public boolean delete(K key) { return data.remove(key) != null; }
    public int size() { return data.size(); }
    @Override public void close() { reaper.interrupt(); }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        try (TtlStore<String, String> s = new TtlStore<>()) {
            s.put("session:42", "nk", Duration.ofMillis(200));
            s.put("config", "v1", null);
            System.out.println(s.get("session:42"));      // Optional[nk]
            Thread.sleep(300);
            System.out.println(s.get("session:42") + " size=" + s.size());   // Optional.empty size=1
        }
    }
}

Adding transactions (begin / commit / rollback, nestable) — a common follow-up:

Java
public class TxStore {
    private static final Object TOMBSTONE = new Object();
    private final Map<String, Object> data = new HashMap<>();
    private final Deque<Map<String, Object>> txs = new ArrayDeque<>();   // innermost on top

    public void begin() { txs.push(new HashMap<>()); }

    public void set(String k, Object v) { (txs.isEmpty() ? data : txs.peek()).put(k, v); }

    public void delete(String k) {
        if (txs.isEmpty()) data.remove(k); else txs.peek().put(k, TOMBSTONE);
    }

    public Optional<Object> get(String k) {
        for (Map<String, Object> layer : txs) {                     // iterates innermost first
            if (layer.containsKey(k)) {
                Object v = layer.get(k);
                return v == TOMBSTONE ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(v);
            }
        }
        return Optional.ofNullable(data.get(k));
    }

    public void rollback() {
        if (txs.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalStateException("no transaction");
        txs.pop();                                                  // discard the innermost layer
    }

    public void commit() {
        if (txs.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalStateException("no transaction");
        Map<String, Object> top = txs.pop();
        Map<String, Object> target = txs.isEmpty() ? data : txs.peek();
        top.forEach((k, v) -> {
            if (v == TOMBSTONE && target == data) data.remove(k);   // apply deletes at the base
            else target.put(k, v);                                  // merge into the parent layer
        });
    }
}

rollback drops the top layer; commit merges it one level down, so a nested commit only becomes durable when the outermost transaction commits.

Extensions to discuss: max size with LRU eviction (combine with the LRU cache), eviction policy as Strategy, persistence (append-only log + snapshot, like Redis AOF/RDB), transactions (begin/commit/rollback with a per-transaction write buffer layered over the main map), pub/sub on key changes (Observer), and sharding by key hash for multiple nodes.

lld-pubsub.tldr:
• Each topic is an append-only log; each subscriber keeps its own offset.
  • Workers wait on a Condition for new data instead of spinning.
  • Offsets can be reset to replay.
  • Extensions: partitions, consumer groups, retention, retries with a DLQ.
lld-pubsub.body:
Requirements: create topics; publishers send messages; multiple subscribers per topic each receive every message; each subscriber consumes at its own pace and can reset its offset to replay (Kafka-like); thread-safe; subscribers process asynchronously.

Design: each topic stores an append-only log (like Kafka); each subscriber has its own offset and a worker thread that waits for new messages using a lock + Condition (no busy spinning). Publishing appends and signals waiting workers.

Java
record Message(String key, String payload, Instant at) {}

interface Subscriber { String id(); void consume(Message m) throws Exception; }

final class Topic {
    final String name;
    private final List<Message> log = new ArrayList<>();
    private final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
    private final Condition newData = lock.newCondition();
    Topic(String name) { this.name = name; }

    void append(Message m) {
        lock.lock();
        try { log.add(m); newData.signalAll(); } finally { lock.unlock(); }
    }

    /** Blocks until a message exists at offset, or the thread is interrupted. */
    Message awaitAt(long offset) throws InterruptedException {
        lock.lock();
        try {
            while (offset >= log.size()) newData.await();
            return log.get((int) offset);
        } finally { lock.unlock(); }
    }
}

final class SubscriberWorker implements Runnable {
    private final Topic topic; private final Subscriber sub;
    final AtomicLong offset = new AtomicLong();
    SubscriberWorker(Topic t, Subscriber s) { topic = t; sub = s; }

    public void run() {
        while (!Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()) {
            long o = offset.get();
            try {
                Message m = topic.awaitAt(o);
                sub.consume(m);
                offset.compareAndSet(o, o + 1);        // commit; a concurrent reset wins
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            } catch (Exception e) {
                System.err.println(sub.id() + " failed at offset " + o + ": " + e.getMessage());
                offset.compareAndSet(o, o + 1);        // skip; a real system would retry then dead-letter
            }
        }
    }
}

public class Broker implements AutoCloseable {
    private final Map<String, Topic> topics = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, SubscriberWorker> workers = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final ExecutorService pool = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor();

    public void createTopic(String name) { topics.putIfAbsent(name, new Topic(name)); }

    public void publish(String topic, String key, String payload) {
        topic(topic).append(new Message(key, payload, Instant.now()));
    }

    public void subscribe(String topic, Subscriber s) {
        SubscriberWorker w = new SubscriberWorker(topic(topic), s);
        if (workers.putIfAbsent(topic + "/" + s.id(), w) != null) throw new IllegalStateException("Already subscribed");
        pool.submit(w);
    }

    public void resetOffset(String topic, String subscriberId, long offset) {
        workers.get(topic + "/" + subscriberId).offset.set(offset);    // replay from offset
    }

    private Topic topic(String name) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(topics.get(name)).orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("No topic " + name));
    }
    @Override public void close() { pool.shutdownNow(); }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        try (Broker b = new Broker()) {
            b.createTopic("orders");
            b.subscribe("orders", new Subscriber() {
                public String id() { return "billing"; }
                public void consume(Message m) { System.out.println("billing <- " + m.payload()); }
            });
            b.subscribe("orders", new Subscriber() {
                public String id() { return "email"; }
                public void consume(Message m) throws InterruptedException { Thread.sleep(50); System.out.println("email <- " + m.payload()); }
            });
            for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) b.publish("orders", "o" + i, "order-" + i);
            Thread.sleep(400);
            b.resetOffset("orders", "billing", 0);        // billing replays all three
            Thread.sleep(200);
        }
    }
}

Extensions: partitions per topic with key-based routing for ordering + parallelism; consumer groups (one worker per partition per group); retention (trim the log by size/time, keeping a base offset); retries with backoff and a dead-letter topic; durable storage (append to segment files); backpressure when subscribers lag.

qa.q: How do you decide between inheritance and composition in LLD?
qa.a: Inheritance only for a true "is-a" relationship where the subtype can substitute the parent everywhere (Liskov). Otherwise compose: hold the varying behaviour in a field behind an interface (Strategy). Composition lets behaviour change at runtime, avoids fragile base classes and deep hierarchies, and keeps classes small.

qa.q: Strategy vs State pattern — what's the difference?
qa.a: Structurally similar (delegate to an interface), different intent. Strategy: the client chooses an interchangeable algorithm (pricing, split type) and it rarely changes during the object's life. State: the object's behaviour changes as its internal state changes, and states trigger transitions to other states (vending machine, booking lifecycle).

qa.q: How would you prevent double booking of seats?
qa.a: Make seat claiming atomic: a conditional update (UPDATE ... SET status='HELD' WHERE id IN (...) AND status='AVAILABLE' and verify the row count), row locks with SELECT FOR UPDATE taken in a consistent order, optimistic versioning, or a Redis SET NX EX per seat for holds. In-memory, lock the seats in sorted order and check-then-hold all-or-nothing under those locks. Holds expire so abandoned carts free seats.

qa.q: How do you make your LLD extensible?
qa.a: Program to interfaces; isolate what varies behind Strategy/State/Factory; keep classes single-purpose; prefer enums with behaviour over string constants; inject dependencies (clock, random, repositories) through constructors; and demonstrate it by adding a new type (e.g. EV spot, new split type) without modifying existing classes.

qa.q: Why inject a Clock or a random supplier?
qa.a: Time and randomness make code non-deterministic and untestable. Injecting Clock lets tests use Clock.fixed/offset to simulate hold expiry or parking duration; injecting an IntSupplier for dice makes game tests repeatable. It's a small detail interviewers notice.

qa.q: When is Singleton appropriate in LLD, and what are its problems?
qa.a: For a single system-wide coordinator (the parking lot, a configuration registry) in a toy setting. Problems: hidden global state, hard to test and mock, concurrency in lazy initialization. In real code prefer one instance managed by DI (Spring beans are singletons by default without the pattern's drawbacks).

qa.q: How would you represent money in your design?
qa.a: As integer minor units (long paise/cents) or BigDecimal with explicit scale and rounding, never double. Keep currency alongside the amount (a Money value object) and handle rounding leftovers deterministically so splits always sum to the total.

qa.q: What makes an LRU cache O(1)?
qa.a: A hash map gives O(1) lookup from key to node, and a doubly linked list ordered by recency gives O(1) move-to-front and O(1) removal of the tail. The map stores node references, so no list traversal is ever needed.

qa.q: How do you make an in-memory design thread-safe without killing throughput?
qa.a: Minimize shared mutable state; use concurrent collections (ConcurrentHashMap and its atomic compute methods); use fine-grained locks (per seat, per spot) instead of one global lock; CAS (AtomicReference.compareAndSet) for single-variable claims; immutable value objects; consistent lock ordering to avoid deadlock; and keep critical sections free of I/O.

qa.q: Walk me through how you'd start a 90-minute machine-coding round.
qa.a: Spend ~10 minutes clarifying requirements and agreeing on scope, sketch entities and a class diagram, then code the models and enums, then the core service with one strategy, then a runnable main demo of the happy path — at ~60 minutes have something working. Use the remaining time for edge cases, validation, concurrency and a second strategy. Working code beats a half-finished perfect design.

cheat.lld-cheatsheet:
How to approach an LLD / machine-coding round

  • Clarify requirements, model entities, define relationships, choose patterns, code core-out, walk a scenario.
  • Graded on modelling, extensibility, correctness, concurrency and code quality.
  • Keep storage in-memory behind repository interfaces.
  • Working code at 60 minutes beats a perfect unfinished design.

Design a parking lot

  • Strategy for spot allocation and pricing; enums map vehicles to spot sizes.
  • Claim spots with an atomic CAS so concurrent gates never double-assign.
  • Track active tickets in a concurrent map; unpark once.
  • Extensions: EV spots, reservations, display boards via Observer.

Design an LRU cache (and LFU) from scratch

  • LRU = HashMap + doubly linked list with sentinels: O(1) get and put.
  • Move to front on access; evict the tail when full.
  • LFU tracks frequency buckets and a running minimum frequency.
  • Production code uses Caffeine (W-TinyLFU).

Design Splitwise (expense sharing)

  • Split types (equal, exact, percent) are Strategies that validate their own input.
  • Store money as paise and assign rounding leftovers deterministically.
  • Keep net balances per user; simplify with a greedy creditor–debtor match (≤ n−1 transfers).
  • Optimal debt minimization is NP-hard.

Design an elevator system

  • Strategy for dispatch; elevators serve stops with the LOOK sweep.
  • Model direction and state explicitly; tick-driven simulation keeps it testable.
  • Prefer elevators already moving toward the call in the same direction.
  • Extensions: capacity, emergency modes, zoning.

Design BookMyShow (movie ticket booking)

  • Seat holds must be atomic and all-or-nothing.
  • Lock seats in a consistent order to avoid deadlocks; holds expire.
  • Confirm only if the hold is still valid; otherwise refund.
  • Distributed version: Redis SET NX EX holds plus a conditional SQL update.

Design a vending machine (State pattern)

  • The State pattern: each state owns its legal actions and transitions.
  • Adding a state means a new class, not editing every switch.
  • Greedy change-making works for canonical coin systems.
  • Handle refunds when change can't be made.

Design Tic-Tac-Toe / Snake & Ladder (game modelling)

  • Row, column and diagonal counters give O(1) win detection.
  • Model turns with a queue of players.
  • Inject randomness (dice) for deterministic tests.
  • Snakes and ladders fit one jump map.

Design an in-memory key-value store with TTL

  • ConcurrentHashMap for data; DelayQueue for active expiry; check on read for lazy expiry.
  • Remove only if the expired entry is still the current one.
  • Extensions: LRU size limits, persistence, transactions, sharding.
  • Mirror Redis's expiry design.

Design an in-memory message queue / pub-sub

  • Each topic is an append-only log; each subscriber keeps its own offset.
  • Workers wait on a Condition for new data instead of spinning.
  • Offsets can be reset to replay.
  • Extensions: partitions, consumer groups, retention, retries with a DLQ.
